name: bento-grid
purpose: A mosaic of unequal cells on one set of shared rules: each cell claims a number of columns and rows, and the rules between them are drawn once so the whole block reads as a single framed surface. It is the layout a marketing page uses when several claims deserve different amounts of room — the alternative to a row of identical tiles.
useWhen: When a set of claims is genuinely unequal and one or two deserve more room than the rest.
As the framed body of a product or platform section, under a `module-header`.
For a logo wall, a client-story band, or any set where a few members carry a headline and the rest carry only a mark.
Whenever the cells hold composed content — copy, media, a control — rather than one repeated shape.
avoidWhen: When every claim carries the same weight → use `card-grid`.
For a row of measured figures → use `stats`, which already draws this grid for numbers.
For a single copy-and-media pairing → use `media-split`.
For a list of questions → use `faq`.
related: `card-grid` — the equal-cell grid with no spans, in the gap or divider register.
`stats` — the same collapsed-rule grid, specialised for figures.
`media-split` — the two-column band when there is one claim, not several.
`registration-frame` — the frame each cell is drawn with.
bestPractices: Size the mosaic so the cells fill the rectangle: count the tracks (`columns` × rows) and check the spans add up, or the grid ends on a gap of bare canvas.
Keep cells in reading order — the grid auto-places in DOM order, so that order is what a screen reader and a keyboard follow, and it is what puts a cell in the track you meant.
Compose real elements inside a cell rather than passing a config array; the cell is a slot, and that is the point of it.
Let the grid draw the rules. Do not add borders inside a cell, or the shared edges double.
Give a cell `variant="none"` + `padded="false"` when its own content paints the cell — a media layer or a brand fill.
Set `href` on a cell when the whole tile is one link, instead of composing a hand-made anchor inside it; the cell then owns the link's focus ring.
Inside a framed page column, set `flush` so the column's rules stay one hairline each.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name for the grid, when the surrounding section does not already name it.

props.name: columns
props.doc: How many columns the mosaic lays out from the medium breakpoint up.

props.name: mobileColumns
props.doc: How many columns the mosaic holds below the medium breakpoint, where every cell claims one of them.

props.name: flush
props.doc: The surrounding frame already draws the grid's outer rules: the grid drops its own top and left ones and lays its right and bottom ones onto the frame's, so a framed column keeps one hairline per edge.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The grid's cells, composed as `BentoGrid.Cell` elements in reading order.
